pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Revert logic to use Popen.communicate. Fixes #80863

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
lib/ansible/module_utils/basic.py

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

This PR:

1. Reverts change to prefer `Popen.communicate`
2. Adds a lot more comments to explain why things are the way they are
3. Aligns selectors logic more closely to `Popen.communicate`, such as a read size that was shown to reduce CPU usage, and use the subprocess preference for the selector implementation.
4. ~Adds a new `bufsize` argument Fixes #80379~

During investigation, I think we've determined that there are cases where a process on some platforms could exit, and stdout/stderr haven't been flushed, and _may_ have data still in them, not quite ready to read from.  I added a commit `loopty loop` that would go back through the loop 1 more time in an attempt to read the pipes after the command had exited, but this added another 2s onto the execution time, so I've reverted it. The specific report where I believe this was the case, had also indicated that increasing the buffer size handled this.

~A backport will need to remove the new `bufsize` argument.~
pr_comments: When will this question fit in? Does the 2.15.2.rc1 version also have the same problem?
Azure Pipelines successfully started running 1 pipeline(s).

I played with rewriting the buffer handling to be thread/coroutine-based, but it'll be much easier to do that robustly after we drop Python 2.7 support. Meantime, IMO this is the best thing to get things mostly working again.

issue_context.title: command / shell never return as of 2.15.0 when stdout/stderr remain held open
issue_context.body:
### Summary

ansible-core 2.14.3 and 2.14.5 work flawlessly.

ansible-core 2.15.0 does not — the [command](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/command_module.html) and [shell](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/shell_module.html) modules never return in situations like those described here:

- iiab/iiab#3588

This has been confirmed on both Debian 11 (x86_64 VM) and 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS (Raspberry Pi 400).

Here's an example of ansible 2.15.0 freezing — as a result of the `./start_asterisk start` command (which works perfectly at the command-line, but no longer with ansible 2.15.0) never returning:

![image](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/assets/2458907/f8a0d89b-f038-4730-93d1-f6a0771fc9d7)

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

command, shell

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version    # BAD VERSION

ansible [core 2.15.0]
  config file = /opt/iiab/iiab/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/root/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/local/ansible/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /root/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /usr/local/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.9.2 (default, Feb 28 2021, 17:03:44) [GCC 10.2.1 20210110] (/usr/local/ansible/bin/python3)
  jinja version = 3.1.2
  libyaml = True

$ ansible --version    # GOOD VERSION

ansible [core 2.14.5]
  config file = None
  configured module search path = ['/root/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/local/ansible/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /root/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /usr/local/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.9.2 (default, Feb 28 2021, 17:03:44) [GCC 10.2.1 20210110] (/usr/local/ansible/bin/python3)
  jinja version = 3.1.2
  libyaml = True

$ ansible --version    # GOOD VERSION

ansible [core 2.14.3]
  config file = /opt/iiab/iiab/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/root/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/local/ansible/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /root/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /usr/local/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.9.2 (default, Feb 28 2021, 17:03:44) [GCC 10.2.1 20210110] (/usr/local/ansible/bin/python3)
  jinja version = 3.1.2
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all

CONFIG_FILE() = /opt/iiab/iiab/ansible.cfg
INTERPRETER_PYTHON(/opt/iiab/iiab/ansible.cfg) = /usr/bin/python3

$ cat /opt/iiab/iiab/ansible.cfg

[defaults]
interpreter_python=/usr/bin/python3
```


### OS / Environment

This has been confirmed on both Debian 11 (x86_64 VM) and 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS (Raspberry Pi 400).

### Steps to Reproduce

Install Asterisk and then FreePBX onto Debian 11 as follows:

- https://github.com/iiab/iiab/blob/master/roles/pbx/tasks/asterisk.yml
- https://github.com/iiab/iiab/blob/master/roles/pbx/tasks/freepbx.yml

CLARIF: PHP 7.4 is required, so newer OS's will not work here.

### Expected Results

Running the exact same command at the prompt (Linux command-line) works.

Ansible should not freeze (the command or shell module never complete with 2.15.0 — unlike with 2.14.x).

### Actual Results

Unfortunately there's no error message, as ansible-core 2.15.0 freezes.

Whereas 2.14.3 and 2.14.5 work perfectly.

Please see details at:

- iiab/iiab#3588

CLARIF:

ansible-core 2.14.6 (released 20min ago) also thankfully works (unlike 2.15.0 !)

~There have been no changes made to the shell/command modules (or their action plugin) between 2.14.6 and 2.15.0~ and I haven't been able to reproduce this using Debian 11 with a simple command or shell task. Are you able to create an isolated reproducer?

Correction: this might be related to https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/80400.

> Are you able to create an isolated reproducer?

Instructions are summarized here:

- iiab/iiab#3589

As we are not the maintainers of (well-known) telephony software Asterisk / FreePBX.

But it's now confirmed by others — repeatable every time (2.14.x always works, 2.15.0 always freezes) if you do invoke a FreePBX installation from Ansible's `command` or `shell` modules.

(Just FYI Internet-in-a-Box was forced to revert all our users from 2.15.0 to 2.14.x as a result.)

We've identified the cause, and arguably it is a misbehaving script that aims to work in place of a service manager by backgrounding the process that it launches.  As a result, the backgrounded process inherits the stdout and stderr of the original process, and does not detach or close them prior to backgrounding the other process, so the CPython `subprocess.Popen.communicate` never completes because it is waiting for `stdout` and `stderr` to be closed.

The PR linked above this comment is reverting the change to use `subprocess.Popen.communicate`, although doing so causes other issues that were resolved by the switch.  So I'm not exactly positive how soon a fix will be merged and released.

Thanks much for explaining:

And as Ansible begins to police certain Linux commands/scripts as Persona Non Grata[*] — then it rather urgently needs to provide a flag (and/or documentation please) explaining how everyone can identify and run "suddenly illegal" Linux commands in other ways :pray:

[*] Possibly for valid security reasons or otherwise, but please do document this on the pages explaining modules {[command](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/command_module.html), [shell](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/shell_module.html), [raw](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/raw_module.html)} with ansible-core 2.15.1 in coming weeks, so Ansible users aren't suddenly left high & dry :/

To be clear, this is a regression[^1]. We sometimes update a vague or overly verbose title to be more to the point. Please don't modify the title after it's clarified; it doesn't change the classification/priority of the issue.

[^1]: as you are using the term, as in "before it worked and now it doesn't"

@s-hertel To be clear, Ansible users are really not interested in being censored.

With all due respect.

> where will this be documented?

Nowhere.

@holta please refrain from making personal attacks. If a core team member changes the title it is to more accurately reflect to ourselves what we believe the problem to be. This is not to censor you, nor to diminish your issue, so please do not modify the title again. 

We are not "policing" commands that users run. Over the years we have had to deal with many such issues (many service systems and other linux environments can be quite a mess) and have already identified the problem here, for which we are working on a fix and thank you for bringing it to our attention. However, if you continue being belligerent, we will consider that a violation of our code of conduct and act accordingly.

@holta this is not a problem if you properly detached from the console (`nohup` is simplest way) or set this up as a proper service and use a service manager to start it. JIC you cannot wait for the fix to be merged and released.

> properly detached from the console (`nohup` is simplest way)

Asterisk and FreePBX being well-established over about 20 years now in the telephony world, yes that's the kind of recommended formulation (`command: nohup ./start_asterisk start` is indeed a workaround with ansible-core 2.15.0) that hopefully can help extricate sincere users everywhere.

Profound thanks for communicating that clearly in the face of this accidental but very serious regression.  @bcoca you're clearly a sincerely non-bureaucratic person of genuine goodwill.  The world depends on people of your stature to stay sane. 😃

Conversely if the wider soul, ethos and purpose of this Ansible forum is regrettably somehow devolving into mischaracterizing, threatening and silencing Ansible users who (1) very earnestly try to get answers, (2) establish working code, and (3) sincerely help others along the way — then that's indeed a _far more unfortunate_ turn of events — that only Ansible's leadership can solve, if they are people of conscience and people of character.

Correction/Clarification for @bcoca:

1) `command: nohup ./start_asterisk start` doesn't work with ansible-core 2.15.0 and 2.15.1 (unless backgrounded Asterisk process happens to be running a priori).

2) Things like `shell: nohup ./start_asterisk start &` also don't work, as the backgrounded Asterisk process is not immediately ready for FreePBX to be installed, for many seconds typically.

Presumably this is because they (mainline telephony software Asterisk / FreePBX) do not detach or close `stdout` and/or `stderr` when they background Asterisk.  As is necessary to install their front-end [FreePBX].  Just FYI for other Asterisk / FreePBX communities trying to get this to work with Ansible.  Capsule Summary: ansible-core 2.15.0 and 2.15.1 both block the official Asterisk / FreePBX install path.
yes, add  `nohup` to the init script as it needs to be at the point of backgrounding

review_comments: There are still numerous ways this can deadlock since we're not pumping stdout/stderr concurrently with the buffer writes.
Yeah, I had debated bringing in the stdin handling from `Popen._communicate` too, but I've never seen a bug report for our use of stdin here, so decided to not tempt fate.
Wouldn't we solve by using `PIPE_BUF` size ?

Also, select/poll are more efficient for a small amount of descriptors, kqueue/epoll are designed to scale a lot better, but this is mostly for a service listening for network connections.  Not sure if you can just avoid the whole thing by using 'select' directly.
Except for the first line, the comment comes from the code of `subprocess` itself.  Just an FYI.

even select/poll choice when dealing with stdin/out is really almost irrelevant.  select is O(highest file descriptor), while poll is O(num of descriptors). mostly old unix variants don't have poll, so select is a 'safe' default', but anything from last 15yrs has poll.

I am thinking that these last 2 should not be 'breaks' but update a counter and continue, then only break when that counter comes here again and exceeds the limit (2 or 3 passes?). This would avoid races with late buffer writes from dead process (unflushed!).  Still, this is optimization for very unlikely corner case, so not going to block PR on it, maybe a later update if we do get reports of this condition.

The hardcoded read size bothers me .. but i know why it is there, python devs tested same on communicate and found it to be the 'best performer'.

Looks good to me to fix the hang, although I feel like the behavior on devel is more predictable, and that a script which wants to run something in the background should either redirect stdout and stderr, or be called with an async task. This/the previous behavior may include some of the stdout/stderr from the background process, but only if it's noisy often enough, whereas on devel it waits for all of it.

Yeah, unfortunately, devel breaks expectations.  I'd be ok with someone doing a follow up that toggles this behavior explicitly.  I cannot think of a good argument name right now. Like `poll_until_exit=True` or something.  But then we have to decide if we extend that `shell`/`command` as well, otherwise it's limited in use.

In the end, I'm unsure if it's really worth it.  Although it makes sense to us, I'm not sure from a user perspective that polling past the process exit would ever be something they would want.

I wish either it would wait for none of the output from a background process (the default, probably what people expect) or all of it but I'm not sure how we'd accomplish the former even with a toggle.
